subject: Re: Eval sprint timeline & variant trade-offs for ACME recommender MAP
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acme.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Turner <ben.turner@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluation sprint + MAP: performance expectations for recommender

Hi Rafael / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We have a short MAP window — procurement wants the evaluation and perf numbers to align with our FYQ4 roll-out rhythm. Key asks from engineering: latency (p95), TTFT for cold-start recommendations, sustained throughput at 1000 req/s, and concurrency behavior with KV cache.

Can Redwood provide a proposed evaluation plan and a target close timeline? Ideally we want concrete variant trade-offs (e.g., quantized gpt-3.5-like vs a larger fp16 variant) so our SREs can validate capacity.

Attached is a starter template for the MAP. Can you confirm scope and a timeline for the benchmark?

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Senior Product Manager, ACME Corp

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation sprint + MAP: performance expectations for recommender

Alicia —

Thanks for the clear asks. Quick proposal below; attaching a detailed MAP workbook (acme_map_v1_timeline.xlsx) and a short perf summary from our lab runs. High level: we’ll run a two-week eval sprint that covers 3 model variants, measure p50/p95 latency, TTFT (initial generation to first token), and throughput curve up to the target 1k rps with concurrency stair-step tests.

Summary plan (high level):
- Week 0 (now): finalize prompt set + sample payload sizes (we’ll use your Prod-ish traces sample).
- Week 1: Controlled lab runs (single-region, 4x RTX A40 nodes) — run A/B perf runs for variants V-small, V-medium, V-large.
- Week 2: Canary in your staging (VPC peering) to validate networking and KV cache warm behavior; capture tail latency under 1000 concurrent users.
- Deliverables: perf CSV, variant comparison doc (ttft + cost est), MAP timeline for procurement.

Quick preview of trade-offs from our initial internal runs (see perf-summary-20260831.csv):
- V-small (8-bit quantized): p50=18ms, p95=95ms, TTFT cold=210ms, throughput saturation ~850 rps, best cost/unit; slight drop in quality on long-tail recommendations.
- V-medium (int8 + partial fp16): p50=25ms, p95=120ms, TTFT cold=270ms, throughput ~1.1k rps; balanced quality/perf.
- V-large (fp16): p50=33ms, p95=200ms, TTFT cold=490ms, throughput ~1.6k rps; highest quality on complex ranking but >2x cost.

Questions for you:
1) Is the 1k rps target steady-state or a burst peak?
2) Any hard SLAs on p95 or TTFT (procurement cares about p95 < 150ms ideally)?

We can shift the canary earlier if procurement requires a faster close. Proposed close target: Sep 15 (contracts signed) if MAP and perf are acceptable.

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Turner <ben.turner@acme.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acme.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation sprint + MAP: performance expectations for recommender

Rafael — quick answers:
- 1k rps is our steady-state expectation for the initial rollout (with 2x burst capacity).
- Procurement: p95 < 150ms is the bar for core recommendation API; we can tolerate higher for batch-only ops.

We’ve uploaded a sample of production traces to your shared Drive link. Please include cost delta estimates per 100M tokens for each variant in your deliverable.

Thanks,
Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Turner <ben.turner@acme.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation sprint + MAP: performance expectations for recommender

Ben / Team —
Following up with concrete measurement plan and acceptance criteria we’ll use inside the MAP workbook. I’ve attached a short PDF that summarizes the variant comparison (variant-comparison-ttft.pdf). Key acceptance tests:
- Cold TTFT: median < 300ms, p95 < 500ms for API traffic
- Sustained throughput: sustain 1k rps for 600s with p95 < 150ms
- Concurrency step test: increase concurrent sessions 100 -> 1.2k to find saturation point
- Quality gating: run 200 labeled prompts (your team) and require no more than 8% degradation vs your current baseline for core metrics (NDCG@10).

Tasking:
- Rafael: execute lab runs and drop perf-summary CSV (ETA Mon Aug 31).
- Neha: coordinate VPC peering + canary network config with ACME (ETA Sep 2).
- Priyom: run quality evals on labeled prompts once lab runs complete.

Marissa
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acme.com>, Ben Turner <ben.turner@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 17:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Evaluation sprint + MAP: performance expectations for recommender

Team — attaching the lab run CSV (perf-summary-20260831.csv) and a quick notes summary below. Ran all three variants against ACME trace (95th percentile token length 78). Environment: 4x A40, continuous batching enabled, KV cache warm for steady-state runs.

Lab highlights:
- V-small (quant 8-bit)
  * p50=20ms, p95=98ms
  * TTFT cold=215ms, warm=48ms
  * Saturation observed ~880 rps (CPU bound on batching orchestrator), degradation in long-tail items (0.6% NDCG drop)
- V-medium (int8+fp16 mix)
  * p50=28ms, p95=125ms
  * TTFT cold=265ms, warm=62ms
  * Sustains ~1.15k rps with p95 ~130ms
- V-large (fp16)
  * p50=35ms, p95=210ms
  * TTFT cold=480ms, warm=95ms
  * Sustains >1.6k rps, best quality (baseline match within 1%)

Initial cost delta per 100M tokens (est): V-small = $420, V-medium = $730, V-large = $1600 (infra + runtime cost estimate). Full breakdown in workbook.

Next steps: scheduling staging canary once Neha confirms VPC peering. Priyom — when you have the labeled set results, we’ll populate the quality gating table.

—Rafael
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acme.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation sprint + MAP: performance expectations for recommender

Alicia / Team —
VPC peering completed (logs in shared Drive). We kicked off the staging canary this morning using V-medium as the first candidate. Early telemetry (first 2 hours): p95 ~135ms at 1k rps steady-state; TTFT cold observed ~280ms for cold sessions, warm=60ms. No security issues surfaced.

If the quality pass from Priyom looks good by Sep 3, our recommendation is to sign the MAP and move to a limited production rollout the week of Sep 13. Procurement: Rafael included the cost delta estimates in the workbook — happy to jump on a call if you want a breakdown.

Neha
Platform Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
